# Starting a tour beside a torn-out window lists its pane twice

## Context

The operator asked on 2026-10-07, as a v13.2 release check: if a user changes the Workstation's perspective by hand and then presses Start tour, does the app first reset to the layout the tour needs, or does it break? It resets the main window only. A pane the user tore into its own window ends up listed twice, and the arrangement can no longer be captured.

This promotes @neo-fable's defect-note from 10:46Z (a code read on `b2db92c5b7`) with a run reproduction.

## The Problem

`TourController.runVisibleTour` (`apps/workstation/view/TourController.mjs:783-786`) enters every visible playback the same way: it assigns `workspace.dockModel = WorkspaceDocument.clone(initialDocument)`, then refreshes main with `geometryOnly: true`. `initialDocument` still lists a pane the user tore into a window. After that assignment, the main document and the pane's vessel both carry the pane.

Reproduction on `dev@b2db92c5b7`: a real `Workspace` bound to its Group; `metrics` torn out through `onTearOutDocumentChange(null, {operation: 'detachItem', itemId: 'metrics'}, …)`; the visible tour entered with a runner that returns at once.

| Read | Before Start | After the tour entry | After `resetTopology()` instead |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Workspaces carrying `metrics` | `workstation-vessel:metrics` | `workstation-main`, `workstation-vessel:metrics` | `workstation-main` |
| `captureTopology()` | | `{topology: null, errors: ['workspaces "workstation-main" and "workstation-vessel:metrics" both carry item "metrics"']}` | |

What follows from it:
- The film's `perspective-capture` cue captures through the same seam, so a film started beside a torn-out window cannot capture its perspective.
- The direct field write fires no commit. Nothing persists, and the history has no row to undo.

An in-window rearrangement is reset correctly today. Only a pane living in another window triggers this, and that is the Workstation's multi-window case.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: the `Workspace.resetTopology()` JSDoc (`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:150-176`): "A pane torn into a window is still listed by `initialDocument`, so restoring that document beside an untouched popup would leave it owned twice — an invalid topology `Persistence` refuses to capture, making a reset that reports success unpersistable." And: "Committing through the Group rather than assigning `dockModel` is what makes the result durable: a direct field write fires no commit event".

- `resetTopology()` (`Workspace.mjs:179-243`) commits `initialDocument` for main and takes every shipped pane back from the other workspaces, in one undoable Group write. It then awaits main's projection and the bound popups'. The Topology toolbar's "Reset to default" calls it.
- Both Start buttons (`startTour`, `startFilmTour`) run through `runVisibleTour`.
- `runSpecTour` (`TourController.mjs:665+`) swaps the document for a probe and restores it afterwards. That is a separate contract.

## The Fix

In `runVisibleTour`, enter through `workspace.resetTopology()` in place of the direct `dockModel` assignment and the geometry-only refresh. If the reset refuses (`reset: false`), the runner does not start: the reset's errors become the receipt's errors, and the caption reads "Tour stopped — …" as for any other stop.

Files:
- `apps/workstation/view/TourController.mjs`
- `test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/TourController.spec.mjs`: the repeated-starts arm counts the entry through `resetTopology`.
- `test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/Workspace.spec.mjs`: the receipt arm's host gains `resetTopology`, plus the torn-out arm.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a shipped pane torn out to its vessel, the visible tour's entry leaves the pane carried by main alone, and `captureTopology()` returns a topology with no errors. Unit test, real `Workspace` and Group.
- [ ] The entry is one Group history row: undo right after it returns the pane to its vessel.
- [ ] A refused reset starts no runner and yields a stopped receipt that carries the reset's errors.
- [ ] The Workstation unit suites pass.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [x] Browser witness, pane comes home: on the fixed head, Euclid's isolated browsers show both Start buttons, after a real tear-out, restore sole main ownership with a valid capture, the same pane identity and an empty retained vessel ([review 5441638430](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19443#pullrequestreview-5441638430)). Fixed by #19443, merged 2026-10-07 as `a67dbc3eb9`.
- [ ] The film's own perspective-capture beat was not reached. A later empty-vessel reuse failure also reproduces on the pre-fix base after a manual reset, so it is not this fix's regression. It is tracked on neomjs/neo#15252 ([6036998586](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15252#issuecomment-6036998586)).

## Out of Scope

- `runSpecTour` and its probe-restore contract.
- Retiring the dense tour or finishing the film (neomjs/neo#15252).
- Closing an emptied vessel window. `resetTopology()` keeps every participant so that its write stays undoable, so a torn-out window stays open, empty.

### Isolated browser witness: both Start buttons enter an invalid topology

Confirmed on 7 October in fresh headless Chrome contexts with an isolated HTTP server and Neural Link bridge. The exercised checkout was `96a30efa`; the `TourController.mjs` and Workstation `Workspace.mjs` blobs match live `dev@b2db92c5` (`f8f207ac` / `470fae7c`).

Reproduction uses the real gesture driver's `executeTearOutStep({itemId: 'metrics', sourceNodeId: 'right-top-tabs'}, {})`, then clicks the actual dense or film Start button without Reset.

| Observation | Dense Start | Film Start |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tear-out | applied; born, sourceReleased and vesselOwns true | same |
| Before Start | capture errors empty; Metrics owned only by its live vessel | same |
| After Start | duplicate ownership error; vessel still live and carrying Metrics | same |
| About 900 ms later | first beat completed; duplicate error persists | same |

The exact capture error in both arms is:

```text
workspaces "workstation-main" and "workstation-vessel:metrics" both carry item "metrics"
```

Dense observations: worker `d73e4c93`, valid pre-Start capture at 10:50:42.265 UTC, invalid post-Start at 10:50:42.300. Film: worker `b811944d`, valid pre-Start at 10:51:10.466, invalid post-Start at 10:51:10.504.

This proves the entry/first-beat defect through both actual browser controls. It does **not** claim complete-tour acceptance or a repaired-path pass. The earlier exploratory arm whose popup returned before Start was excluded. The positive repair should preserve one Metrics owner and valid capture; an empty retained vessel is allowed by the undoable-reset contract.

All isolated browsers, server and bridge were stopped; tracked state remains clean. No operator session or installed plane was used.
